newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco deal likely to address insurance issue.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco deal likely to address insurance issue.

text.p: Any settlement of tobacco litigation is likely to include a decision by the state attorneys general about whether to pursue insurers for coverage.

"I would think once there is a settlement, the hope would be that there would be a settlement that is global in nature and would satisfy all of the concerns," Louisiana Attorney General Richard Ieyoub said.
Ieyoub said it was possible, but "probably not likely," that a tobacco settlement would be reached without a decision on the insurance issue.
Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore last week told Reuters he hoped to know within two weeks whether a settlement of tobacco industry litigation could be reached.
The attorneys general earlier this month formed working groups to consider several issues, including whether there is insurance to cover claims against the industry.

Ieyoub, who heads the committee, said a team of outside lawyers who specialize in policyholder representation has reviewed policies provided by Philip Morris Cos Inc and believes there may be coverage.
"We feel pretty confident there is some coverage," Ieyoub said.
Insurers, however, argue that policies sold to tobacco companies after the mid-1960s specifically exclude payment for loses related to the harmful effects of smoking.

The committee, which includes several other state attorneys general and the policyholder specialists from Washington D.C. law firm McKenna & Cuneo, last week met with tobacco industry representatives in New York City to discuss why coverage may exist.
Ieyoub said he is now awaiting a response from the tobacco industry and is continuing to explore the issue of insurance coverage.
The attorneys general then will decide whether to push the insurers for coverage.
"I think we should be hearing something very soon about the insurance issue," Ieyoub said. "I definitely think that. I would suppose that would be in the very near future," he said.
One of the decisions, Ieyoub said, could be to include the insurers in the tobacco settlement talks.
But, he said it was far to early to say how much this could cost the insurance industry.
